Cheuko's background in martial arts was evident from his online clips showcasing him working through various disciplines, including boxing and Muay Thai. The Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu skills of the Ruotolo twins were likely to be a challenge for someone with a similar foundation. The impromptu lesson took place in an unconventional setting, as Tye noted that there wasn't even a mat underneath their feet. However, Cheuko's willingness to adapt and roll with the situation was apparent. His eagerness to learn was met with enthusiasm from the Ruotolo twins, who appreciated the opportunity to share their expertise. The twins' experience in teaching was put to good use as they guided Cheuko through the intricacies of grappling. This unique encounter allowed them to connect with someone from a different background and showcase their skills in a more relaxed environment. Tye's upcoming challenge is set to take place on November 6, where he will face Christian "The Warrior" Lee for the lightweight belt at The Inner Circle 37. The younger Ruotolo twin has been making a name for himself in the martial arts world, boasting an impressive 10-0 record across submission grappling and MMA disciplines. His six submission grappling wins have showcased his skills in this area, while his four stoppage victories in MMA demonstrate his prowess in the octagon. With Kade's strong performance on the grandest stage of martial arts, he is poised to take a significant leap forward in the division if he emerges victorious against his opponent. articles.title: Linda Fargo's Journey to Becoming a Fashion Icon
articles.summary: Linda Fargo rose through the ranks in the fashion industry after starting her career as a display artist at Macy's, where she worked with designers like Matsuda and Kansai Yamamoto.
articles.content: Linda Fargo's journey to becoming one of the most influential figures in fashion began far from the catwalks of New York City. Growing up in Wisconsin, she dreamed of leaving the Midwest and making her mark on the art world. A self-taught artist with a passion for found objects and assemblage, Fargo's creative vision was shaped by her love of repurposing and reimagining discarded materials. Her skills in manipulating disparate elements to create something new and cohesive were a testament to her innovative spirit. Despite her artistic inclinations, Fargo struggled to make a name for herself as a fine artist. The art world was highly competitive, and she found it challenging to stand out from the crowd. In search of a more practical outlet for her creativity, Fargo began exploring other career paths that would allow her to utilize her skills in a different context. Fargo's entry into the fashion industry was unexpected, but it was also an opportunity for growth and development. She landed her first job at Macy's in the display department, where she quickly learned the ins and outs of creating visually stunning window displays. The art school graduate brought her unique perspective to the role, using her skills in assemblage to create intricate and captivating displays that drew customers into the store. Her passion for fashion was sparked by working with high-end designers like Matsuda and Kansai Yamamoto, who were featured prominently at Macy's during this period. As Fargo settled into her new role, she quickly rose through the ranks, becoming production manager for the window director within a few years. By 1984, she had taken on the position of window director herself, overseeing the creation of iconic displays that showcased the latest designer collections. Designing thousands of windows over her lifetime has been a defining aspect of Linda Fargo's career. Each one has its own story and she could talk about them endlessly. The process involves creating an immersive experience that transports customers into a fantasy world, often using clever ideas to showcase designer collections. One notable example was the Perry Ellis window where mannequins were transformed into falconers with birds perched on their arms. This creative concept showcased the brand's ability to push boundaries and think outside the box. The attention to detail in such displays is what sets Linda Fargo apart from other professionals in her field. Working on a project for the American Ballet Theater required her to venture out of the city, visiting a Brooklyn warehouse that stored costumes and props. Upon entering the vast space, she was struck by the sheer number of tutus stacked like pancakes. It was clear that only the most prominent ballerinas received the new, pristine ones. In another instance, Linda Fargo had an idea for an American Ballet Theater window that involved using a smoke machine to make mannequins appear as if they were floating. To execute this vision, she and her team secured the help of a local vendor on Canal Street who lent them the equipment. However, things quickly took an unexpected turn. As they set up inside the window, closing the door behind them to prevent the smoke from escaping, the machine suddenly malfunctioned. The team found themselves trapped inside, writing "HELP on the glass and pounding on the doors as the smoke filled the space. The associate finally arrived through the fine jewelry department entrance, opening the door for the team's safe escape. However, their ordeal was far from over, as the smoke continued to seep into the store through cracks in the window. The incident led them to abandon that particular display, but they ultimately decided to proceed with the rest of the windows despite the chaos caused by the malfunctioning machine. As my career in fashion progressed, I found myself at the helm of creating visually stunning displays that captivated customers' attention. My team would often joke that I was the mastermind behind our store's window displays, likening me to a Hollywood director. I took pride in pushing the boundaries and experimenting with new ideas, always striving for perfection. The pace of work was frenetic, but it was exhilarating to see an idea come to life within a matter of days. It was this fast-paced environment that helped me develop my skills as a project manager, learning how to delegate tasks and meet tight deadlines. One of the most valuable lessons I learned during this period was the importance of adaptability. When unexpected setbacks occurred, such as the malfunctioning machine that caused chaos in our window display area, we had to think on our feet and adjust our plans accordingly. The experience taught me to be flexible and not take things too seriously, even when faced with adversity. It also instilled in me a sense of responsibility, knowing that my team was counting on me to deliver results. After leaving Macy's at the age of 30, I landed a coveted role as VP of visual for another iconic department store. The opportunity came with its own set of challenges, but it also offered a chance to apply the skills and knowledge I had acquired during my time at Macy's. The company was known for its high-end merchandise and exceptional customer service, making it an exciting place to work. However, this experience would soon come to an end due to unforeseen circumstances that would change the course of my career once again. The company I was working for at the time had an enormous retail presence, with 850 stores across the globe. This experience taught me a valuable lesson about my own career aspirations: I don't thrive in environments that prioritize scale above all else. I recall having a great deal of respect for The Gap, but what I ultimately sought was a more intimate connection to the people and products involved in the fashion industry. As I navigated various roles over the years, I began to realize that sometimes it's just as important to learn what you don't want from your career as it is to discover what you do want. This realization led to a period of introspection for me, which can be described as an existential crisis. In an effort to shake things up and take control of my own destiny, I decided to cold call Bergdorf Goodman in New York City. I compiled a portfolio of ideas and sent it through the mail, not knowing what to expect. To my surprise, I received a response from the company's president at the time, Dawn Mello, inviting me for an interview. This led to a new opportunity for me: being hired as the visual director at Bergdorf Goodman in 1996 was a pivotal moment in my career. Upon joining the team, I was struck by the fact that the store had become somewhat stagnant, it was a sleeping beauty" in need of revitalization. I saw an abundance of potential, and my first priority was to revamp the window displays. As the visual director, I knew that these would be the first impression that customers would have of our brand. As I began working on those initial window displays during my first summer at Bergdorf Goodman, I found myself captivated by the beauty of the store's exterior. The way the street lamps lit up along Fifth Avenue in the evening was truly magical, and it made me feel grateful to be a part of such an iconic brand. The window displays at Bergdorf Goodman were always a key part of the shopping experience, and as a young creative director, I had the opportunity to play a significant role in shaping their design. One of my early projects involved creating a circus-themed display that featured an array of different characters, each showcasing a unique aspect of fashion. This approach allowed us to showcase multiple brands and designers at once, which has since become a hallmark of Bergdorf's window displays. Today, the store still uses this multi-brand approach for most of its windows, reserving single-brand takeovers for major events like designer launches. For example, when Matthieu Blazy unveiled his New York collection for Chanel, the entire Fifth Avenue storefront was transformed into a cohesive brand experience. As a creative director, I loved pushing the boundaries of what was possible in our window displays. One particularly memorable project involved creating the illusion of a subway running through the windows, complete with miniature trains and tracks. When Jim Gold offered me the women's fashion office in 2006, it was a turning point in my career. As president, he had taken note of my skills as a creative director and saw potential for me to excel in an editorial role. As I transitioned from window displays to fashion editing, I began to appreciate the importance of discovering new designers and emerging talent. With over 5,000 fashion shows under my belt, I've developed a keen eye for spotting hidden gems, and it's a skill that has served me well in my current role. As a senior executive at Bergdorf Goodman, I've had to adapt my approach to stay ahead in the ever-evolving fashion industry. In today's sophisticated and large-scale business, the stakes are higher than ever before, and it can be daunting for young designers to navigate these treacherous waters. However, as someone with over 5,000 fashion shows under their belt, I've developed a keen eye for spotting hidden gems, and it's this skill that has served me well in my current role. I believe the industry needs to prioritize the creativity of its designers, supporting them every step of the way, while also being discerning about what we choose to showcase. This delicate balance is crucial in an era where there are countless options for consumers, making our curated approach all the more valuable. articles.summary: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson suffered a chest injury during the Week 8 "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Carolina Panthers.
articles.content: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson suffered a chest injury during the first half of the Week 8 "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Carolina Panthers. The severity of the injury prompted his departure from the game and led to precautionary tests at a hospital near Lambeau Field. Watson's condition was assessed, and after clearing medical protocols, he was given clearance to return to the game. He arrived back at the stadium in an ambulance and quickly made his way into the locker room to prepare for re-entry. Upon emerging onto the sideline, Watson had additional padding around his ribs, indicating that the injury required extra protection. When questioned by teammates about the nature of the injury, he pointed to the lower right side of his chest. Watson's decision to return to play was a personal one, driven by his desire to be on the football field. In an interview with Prime Video's Kaylee Hartung after the game, he reflected on the experience. The Packers' coaching staff had initially deemed Watson questionable for re-entry, but ultimately allowed him to resume playing once they were satisfied that his condition was stable enough to do so without further risk of injury. Watson's hospital visit was triggered by blood he spat up after sustaining his chest injury, prompting the medical staff to take him in for further evaluation. Fortunately, tests revealed no internal bleeding, paving the way for his return to action. The injury occurred during a pivotal play in the first half, a 53-yard reception that set up the Packers' second touchdown of the night. Watson's collision with Panthers cornerback Will Lee III also left Lee injured, and he was subsequently ruled doubtful to return due to a hamstring issue. Watson had been dominating on offense before his departure, leading all receivers in the first half with six catches for 100 yards. His ability to outmaneuver the struggling Panthers defense allowed quarterback Jordan Love to complete an impressive 17 of his first 20 passes. The Packers wasted little time calling Watson's number upon his return from the hospital, and while he didn't come down with the catch on his first play back, he did manage a pair of receptions in the fourth quarter. Those catches proved crucial, as one of them converted a key third-down situation. Watson's second grab of the quarter nearly sealed the game for Green Bay, as it allowed the team to drain valuable time off the clock and limit the Panthers' final possession to mere seconds. The Packers' coaching staff had clearly been monitoring Watson's condition closely, allowing him to re-enter the game once they were satisfied that his injury was stable enough to do so without further risk. Matthew Golden's performance shone brightly as he took over as the top receiver for the Packers after Christian Watson's departure due to injury. He made an immediate impact by snagging a touchdown pass on Green Bay's first possession without Watson. Golden had previously dropped a crucial pass that could have resulted in another score, but he redeemed himself with this pivotal catch. Watson's history of injuries has been a recurring theme throughout his NFL career. In addition to the recent chest injury and hospital visit, he has suffered from several other significant injuries including three hamstring strains, an ankle sprain, and multiple knee bruises. He also experienced a concussion during his rookie season in 2022, a setback that added to his growing list of health concerns. The cumulative effect of these injuries has been substantial, with Watson missing 20 games over the course of five seasons in the league. His inability to play a full season is a testament to the challenges he has faced on and off the field, making each game a significant accomplishment for the talented but injury-prone player. articles.title: Benjamin Netanyahu Faces Election Setback in Israel
articles.summary: The opposition is poised to potentially gain a majority in parliament if they form an alliance with Arab-led parties, marking a significant shift in Israeli politics.
articles.content: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing a significant setback in the country's recent elections. His party, Likud, has made unsubstantiated claims that Arab-led parties stole the election, potentially with foreign assistance, after losing its majority in parliament. The opposition has accused Netanyahu of trying to delegitimize the election by demonizing the Arab population, which has been gaining political influence in Israel. If other opposition parties were to form an alliance with Arab-led parties, they could potentially gain a majority in parliament, marking a significant shift in Israeli politics. According to the latest results from election officials, Netanyahu's bloc secured 53 seats out of 120 in the Knesset, while his main opposition won 48. Arab-led parties made a historic showing by securing the remaining 19 seats. This outcome has raised concerns about the future of Netanyahu's leadership and the balance of power in Israel. The final count is complete, but the results still need to be certified and submitted to the country's president next Wednesday. In the meantime, Netanyahu's party continues to spread claims of malfeasance by Arab-led parties, with some accusations even suggesting foreign interference. The Israeli election commission has announced that it will investigate allegations of foreign interference in the recent elections. The investigation is based on classified intelligence and was revealed as the commission released its preliminary results earlier this week. Netanyahu's party has responded to the news by leveling accusations at Arab-led parties, with some claims even suggesting that foreign powers are behind the alleged malfeasance. In a statement, Netanyahu's party claimed that the elections had been "stolen, although it provided no evidence to support this claim. The allegations of foreign interference have also targeted Qatar, which has been accused by members of Netanyahu's party of seeking to influence the election outcome. However, Qatar has denied these claims as ridiculous and dangerous. Netanyahu's claims of malfeasance by Arab-led parties have taken a new turn as he attempts to shift attention from his own party's alleged ties to Qatar. This move is seen as an attempt to discredit potential alliances between his opponents and the Arab parties. Critics argue that Netanyahu's accusations are an attempt to further marginalize Arab citizens, who make up 20% of Israel's population but are often viewed with suspicion due to their sympathies with other Palestinians. The Likud party has been accused of using such tactics in the past to undermine support for Arab-led parties. The Shin Bet investigation into alleged foreign interference in the election is ongoing, with the agency seeking to calm tensions by stating that its probe was not intended to cast aspersions on any particular group of voters. This assertion comes amidst growing concerns over Netanyahu's attempts to delegitimize the results of the election. In a letter to a concerned member of parliament, the elections committee emphasized that allegations of widespread electoral integrity issues are unfounded and baseless. The committee has requested findings from the Shin Bet within a week, as it continues its investigation into the matter. The investigation into election interference has taken center stage in Israel's post-election landscape. Tensions are running high as allegations of malfeasance swirl around Arab-led parties, which have been accused by Netanyahu's party of attempting to steal the election. Campaign attacks against Arab-led parties, coupled with widespread discontent over Netanyahu and his far-right government, have fueled unprecedented voter turnout among Arabs in recent elections. The head of the Democrats party, Yair Golan, has claimed that Netanyahu is trying to undermine the election results through a smear campaign targeting the Arab public. The Joint List party has echoed these sentiments, stating bluntly that Netanyahu is working to steal the election. In response, Mansour Abbas, leader of the Ra'am party, has welcomed the investigation into election interference and denied any involvement in the case. Instead, he has accused Netanyahu's government of a campaign of incitement. President Isaac Herzog has weighed in on the controversy, describing it as a sensitive moment" that requires a full investigation to ensure no community is unfairly targeted or tarnished for exercising its democratic rights. The Israeli election continues to unfold with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remaining at the helm despite his party's claims of electoral malfeasance by Arab-led parties. Critics warn that if Netanyahu loses office, he will face accountability for yearslong corruption allegations and an inquiry into the security failures leading up to the devastating Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023. This would be a significant setback for him as he has sought to avoid such consequences at all costs. Arab-led parties could assert their growing power in the next parliament by supporting other Netanyahu opponents, potentially allowing them to elect a new speaker and control the legislative agenda before a new government is formed. Eisenkot has expressed openness to joining forces with Arab-led parties under certain conditions. Meanwhile, Ahmad Tibi of the Joint List revealed that the opposition bloc had reached out to him about replacing the Knesset speaker, and his party would support their candidate. Small rallies have taken place in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem in support of a coalition including Arab-led parties, marking a significant shift from the past when no Arab party had joined a coalition government until 2021. If a new government cannot be formed after multiple attempts, Israel's election process may lead to another vote early next year. This scenario has become increasingly likely as efforts to establish a coalition continue to falter. New elections would raise further questions about voter turnout, particularly among Arab citizens who made up a significant portion of those who cast their ballots in the previous poll. articles.title: Global restoration project creates 1 million jobs worldwide
articles.summary: Global efforts to restore ecosystems are underway at a significant scale, with 252 million hectares of land across 149 countries being restored. This vast restoration effort has created...
articles.content: Global efforts to restore ecosystems are underway at a significant scale, with 252 million hectares of land across 149 countries being restored. This vast restoration effort has created more than 1 million green jobs, making it the largest documented global restoration project to date. To meet ambitious targets set for 2030, however, action must accelerate rapidly. A particular focus is needed on restoring freshwater, marine and coastal ecosystems, which are essential for the health of our planet. Furthermore, annual investment in restoration efforts needs to increase dramatically, with a fourfold rise required over current levels. The report, "Nature's comeback, scaling ecosystem restoration for people and planet", provides the first comprehensive assessment of global progress towards restoring 1 billion hectares of degraded land by 2030. This target is part of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which aims to ensure that at least 30% of degraded ecosystems are under effective restoration by 2030. The report highlights the importance of meeting these targets in order to protect biodiversity and mitigate the effects of climate change. It emphasizes that increased investment in ecosystem restoration is not only crucial for environmental health but also has economic benefits, potentially generating an estimated 32 million new jobs worldwide by 2030. Launched at a high-level event during the U.N. Biodiversity Conference (COP17), the report was co-published by several international organizations, including the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the U.N. Environment Programme. The event recognized five initiatives from around the world as U.N. World Restoration Flagships, highlighting successful restoration projects in China, Colombia, Ethiopia, Italy, and the United States. The global movement to restore nature is gaining momentum, with a growing number of initiatives spanning national programs, cities, schools, businesses, and community projects. This diverse range of efforts has helped expand the partnership network of the U.N. Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, which now encompasses over 300 organizations from all regions. These partnerships have been instrumental in driving restoration efforts across various ecosystems worldwide. According to available data, Asia is leading the charge with a significant portion of documented restoration areas, accounting for approximately 192.2 million hectares (474.9 million acres) out of the total area under restoration. Regional disparities in restoration activity are not necessarily indicative of performance but rather reflect differences in land area, monitoring capabilities, and reporting capacities. Africa, Europe, North and Central America, South America, and Oceania also have notable restoration areas, with 36.3 million hectares (89.7 million acres), 9.1 million hectares (22.5 million acres), 5.8 million hectares (14.3 million acres), 5.4 million hectares (13.3 million acres), and 3.2 million hectares (7.9 million acres) respectively. The sheer scale of restoration activity varies significantly across regions, with Asia accounting for the largest share. This disparity is largely due to regional differences in land area and capacities for monitoring and reporting rather than a reflection of restoration performance. Restoration efforts are crucial for ensuring food and water security, climate resilience, jobs, and overall well-being across all ecosystems. Restoring just a small fraction of global priority areas could have a significant impact on the environment. According to research, recovering 15% of these areas could capture and store up to 30% of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions since the Industrial Revolution, helping to avoid 60% of species extinctions. The United Nations has documented several successes in its World Restoration Flagships program, which showcases recovery efforts for various species. For instance, mountain gorillas in East Africa are making a comeback, as are jaguars in Brazil, snow leopards in Kyrgyzstan, and Ganges River dolphins in India. While restoration progress varies across different ecosystems and countries, some areas have made significant strides. The global target to restore 30% of degraded terrestrial ecosystems by 2030 is nearly halfway met. China leads the way with a substantial area under restoration, followed closely by Mongolia and Kazakhstan. However, not all ecosystems are faring as well. Progress in freshwater, marine, and coastal ecosystems has been much slower, despite these areas being some of the most rapidly degrading environments. Only a small fraction of these ecosystems have been documented as being under restoration. The number of countries reporting implemented wetland restoration or rehabilitation programs has more than doubled since 2022, indicating growing momentum in this area. However, the limited reporting for aquatic restoration may result in an underestimate of the actual progress being made. The restoration efforts underway to protect nature's resilience and human well-being are showing progress, but more needs to be done to meet targets. A significant increase in funding is required to achieve these goals, with a fourfold rise in annual financing from $64 billion to $296 billion by 2030. The largest financial investments will be needed for agroforestry initiatives at an estimated $87 billion per year, followed closely by restorative reforestation ($52 billion), peatland restoration ($44 billion) and seagrass restoration ($28 billion). Governments must take a more proactive approach to addressing the drivers of ecosystem degradation, said Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) Secretariat. This includes investing in monitoring mechanisms to ensure the long-term effectiveness of restoration efforts. To achieve lasting success, restoration initiatives must be sustained beyond 2030 and enable the recovery of ecosystem integrity and biodiversity. Secure land tenure, meaningful community participation, and respect for Indigenous peoples' rights are essential components of durable restoration. The next phase of the U.N. Decade on Ecosystem Restoration will require a shift towards "restoration economies" that can support ecological recovery, livelihoods, and long-term value at scale. This involves moving beyond individual projects to create sustainable systems capable of sustaining ecological benefits over time. Restoration efforts are making progress, but more needs to be done quickly to meet ecological goals. The pace of restoration must accelerate to achieve sustainability over time, according to a recent report from the United Nations Environment Programme. This requires moving beyond individual projects and creating systems that can maintain their benefits for years to come. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-10-efforts-faster.html

articles.title: Microplastic Aging Process Revealed in Groundbreaking Study

articles.content: A groundbreaking study has shed new light on the aging process of microplastics in the environment, revealing how these tiny plastic particles interact with other contaminants as they break down over time. Microplastics are small pieces of plastic that measure less than 5 millimeters in length, and researchers have been studying their behavior to better understand their impact on the environment. This latest study focused on three common types of polymer chemicals: polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, and polypropylene. As these microplastics age, they undergo changes that can affect how they interact with other substances in their surroundings. The researchers found that microplastics have a tendency to bind to copper, which is a toxic substance that can harm aquatic life like fish, amphibians, and invertebrates. Microplastics can act as environmental carriers for copper, altering its movement and increasing toxicity when it is discharged into lakes and rivers through wastewater plants. This has significant implications for the health of aquatic ecosystems, which are already vulnerable to pollution from human activities. Wastewater treatment plants are significant contributors to plastic pollution in natural waters, allowing plastic particles to enter aquatic ecosystems. Researchers at Baylor University have developed a method to simulate the aging process of microplastics (MPs) that occur during wastewater treatment. They achieved this by accelerating chemical oxidation of three common MP polymers, mimicking the conditions found in these plants where plastics tend to accumulate. The team's experiments revealed that both pristine and oxidized MPs can attach to copper across all three studied polymers. This suggests that microplastics can interact with contaminants like copper regardless of their condition. However, the researchers warn that the role of microplastics as vectors for copper ions in real-world environments may be more complex or variable than observed under these accelerated conditions and should be viewed with caution. The accelerated aging process used in this study allowed researchers to simulate the effects of environmental stressors on microplastics over time. This enabled them to examine how changes in physical properties and chemical cargo might influence interactions between microplastics and contaminants such as copper ions. The research suggests that aged microplastics can indeed act as vectors for copper ions, potentially altering their bioavailability and risk profile. However, the findings also highlight the complexity of these interactions, underscoring the need for further investigation into real-world environmental contexts. articles.title: Construction Underway for New Sculpture Garden on National Mall
articles.summary: Workers are smoothing freshly poured concrete in West Potomac Park to prepare for two traditional Uzbek open-sided pavilions and life-size statues of notable Americans.
articles.content: Workers in West Potomac Park just off the National Mall were seen smoothing freshly poured concrete in early September. The area was fenced off, indicating a major construction project underway. It appears to be part of a larger initiative to create a new sculpture garden. The installation of two traditional Uzbek open-sided pavilions, known as aywans, is taking place at the site. Aywans feature elaborately carved wooden columns and roofs, adding an exotic touch to the area. The structures are being built in preparation for the installation of life-size statues of notable Americans. The federal call for artists specified that the statues must be realistic and classical, made from traditional materials such as marble, granite, bronze, copper, or brass. This requirement reflects a desire to create a sense of timelessness and permanence. The National Garden of American Heroes is intended to commemorate important figures in American history. As a city built on symbolism, Washington D.C.'s landscape is ever-changing. The distinction between planned projects and already-completed installations can be blurry at times. The National Mall has long been a site where ideas about America's identity are displayed for all to see. The Hirshhorn Museum's new sculpture garden is a significant addition to the National Mall, located just over a mile northeast of where the aywans were being installed. This project marks the culmination of Melissa Chiu's 12-year tenure as director of the Hirshhorn Museum, which ended when she took on the role of director at the Guggenheim in New York in September. The sculpture garden will feature nearly 60 works of art spanning over a century, including pieces from the museum's founder Joseph H. Hirshhorn's collection and recent acquisitions by diverse artists working today. The garden is designed to complement the more classical National Gallery of Art, with its unique collection showcasing American identity through the lens of modern and contemporary sculpture. The Hirshhorn Museum's unique architecture was designed by Gordon Bunshaft as a standalone sculpture, a monumental concrete cylinder set apart from the neoclassical buildings surrounding it. This bold design choice aimed to break away from traditional museum aesthetics and create a distinct identity for the institution. As the new Sculpture Garden takes shape, visitors are being encouraged to engage with contemporary art in innovative ways. The garden's design is meant to complement the National Gallery of Art, showcasing American identity through modern and contemporary sculpture. This approach reflects the Hirshhorn's commitment to pushing boundaries and making art more accessible to a wider audience. The museum's focus on accessibility has been a key aspect of its programming, with staff working to reduce physical and intellectual barriers that might deter visitors from engaging with challenging works. By rethinking everything from wall texts to educational materials, the Hirshhorn aims to create an inclusive environment where visitors can appreciate art on their own terms. In line with this approach, the museum has developed a mobile guide called Hirshhorn Eye, which allows visitors to hear artists discuss their work directly. This initiative reflects the institution's commitment to putting the artist at the forefront of the visitor experience and facilitating meaningful connections between viewers and creators. The museum's emphasis on accessibility has also led it to reevaluate its voice and tone in engaging with visitors. By shifting from a more formal, didactic approach to one that is more conversational and inclusive, the Hirshhorn aims to create a welcoming environment where everyone can feel at ease exploring contemporary art. The Hirshhorn Museum's efforts to engage a broader audience extend beyond its physical walls through digital initiatives and multimedia projects. This approach is particularly relevant given the museum's diverse visitor base, which includes individuals who may not typically frequent contemporary art institutions. Many visitors arrive at the museum with little expectation of encountering world-class modern and contemporary art due to its free admission and prime location on the National Mall. The Hirshhorn Museum's new Sculpture Garden is undergoing significant changes, with many of its original works being returned to their former glory. Iconic pieces like Rodin's The Burghers of Calais and Monument to Balzac will be reinstalled alongside Matisse's complete series of The Backs I-IV. These additions will be joined by a selection of modern and contemporary art from renowned artists such as Moore, Giacometti, Barbara Hepworth, David Smith, and Lucio Fontana. The museum has also been acquiring new works that expand its geographical and cultural scope. Recent commissions include pieces by Lauren Halsey, Raven Halfmoon, Mark Grotjahn, Liz Larner, Woody De Othello, Izumi Kato, Pedro Reyes, and Chatchai Puipia. These additions will further enrich the garden's diverse offerings. Among the new installations is a poignant piece called Wish Tree, created by artist Mungo Thomson. This striking work invites visitors to leave behind handwritten wishes for peace, creating a sense of community and shared longing among those who visit. Another notable addition is Elmgreen Dragset's Eight, an imposing 28-foot-tall vertical swimming pool complete with diving board, ladder, and lights. The new Sculpture Garden will be a marked departure from its original design by Gordon Bunshaft. The austere setting of the old garden was characterized by a lack of shade or greenery, with visitors entering from the Mall having to descend a flight of stairs to encounter a 10-foot concrete wall. However, subsequent interventions by landscape architect Lester Collins have softened the space, adding canopy trees and more vegetation to create a more welcoming atmosphere. The Hirshhorn Museum's Sculpture Garden underwent significant changes in recent years, addressing infrastructure issues and revamping its design. To tackle these challenges, architect Chiu collaborated with artist Hiroshi Sugimoto, who had a prior connection to the museum through a 2006 exhibition of his work. Sugimoto envisioned the garden as an interactive space where visitors could engage with art, rather than just viewing it from afar. articles.title: Top-handle Handbags Make Triumphant Return to Fashion Runways This Fall
articles.summary: Designers have been featuring models carrying one- or two-strapped purses that recall the classic handheld style, breathing new life into a once-derided category.
articles.content: The top-handle handbag trend has made a triumphant return to fashion runways this fall, dominating shows in key style capitals around the world. Designers have been featuring models carrying one- or two-strapped purses that recall the classic handheld style, breathing new life into a once-derided category. Gone are the prim and stodgy connotations associated with top-handle bags; this season's offerings showcase a diverse range of shapes and styles. The latest crop of top-handle handbags defies any single aesthetic, instead embracing an eclectic mix of silhouettes that cater to various tastes and preferences. From elongated east-west designs inspired by current accessory trends to slouchy, relaxed styles that exude effortless chic, there's something for everyone. In addition to their stylish appeal, these bags also prioritize practicality, with roomy totes and bucket bags ideal for everyday use, whether commuting to work or running errands on the weekend. A top-handle bag offers a stylish alternative to the standard clutch, combining the elegance of a small handbag with the added convenience of a strap for carrying. Beyond shape and design, top-handle bags also come in a variety of textures that add depth and interest to any outfit. Suede and velvet are particularly popular choices for cold weather, lending a luxurious feel to even the simplest of ensembles. In addition to their tactile appeal, these bags also boast bold colors and prints that provide a refreshing contrast to the more subdued tones often seen during winter. Whether you prefer classic neutrals or statement-making hues, there's a top-handle bag to suit your personal style. A range of styles are available to cater to different tastes and occasions, from spacious and functional designs ideal for work or travel, to softer, slouchier shapes perfect for everyday wear. The Row's Agnes bag and Coach's Empire are two excellent options for work bags, available in various sizes to suit different needs. Croc-embossed leather can instantly elevate a handbag's style, adding visual interest without relying on flashy embellishments or hardware. The glossy surface of this finish is particularly striking when paired with rich shades such as deep burgundy and oxblood, reminiscent of reptile-inspired textures. Suede handbags possess an inherently luxurious quality, thanks to their soft, velvety surfaces that add depth to any outfit. This fabric complements contrasting materials like wool, denim, and leather nicely, but requires more care than smooth leather - consider treating it with a protective spray before its first use and avoiding exposure to rain. The Lady bag stands out for its elegant proportions and sophisticated shape, defined by shiny hardware, frame closures, and sculptural handles. Its understated design makes it an excellent choice for those who prefer minimalistic accessories, yet still want a polished look. For those who require more space, larger top-handle bags are available for everyday use. In contrast, smaller compact versions of these bags can be chosen for evening events, offering a polished look without the bulk. The Slouchy Bag is an option for a more effortless appearance, featuring supple materials that allow it to fold and drape naturally, creating an undone effect. This softer construction also provides greater flexibility when packing essentials. Vogue : https://www.vogue.com/article/top-handle-bags
